newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real ends flat on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real ends flat on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real closed flat at 1.0275 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.0265 to 1.0315, dealers said.

The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.0265 reais and selling at 1.0315 reais in a morning auction. The move was already expected by the market, they added said.
The previous mini-band, set on Oct 25, was between 1.0260 and 1.0310 reais.
Dealers said trading was slow after an airplane carrying financial executives crashed in Sao Paulo early Thursday, killing 103 people.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Thursday deficit of $80 million.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.04 percent to end at 1.0319.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.095, according to traders.
